notes:
Short summary: Polymath Copilots builds an IDE-native assistant for enterprise dev teams. Primary ask: deterministic code completions with model/version pinning and reproducible rollout behavior. Key quotes from product lead: "we need predictable completions across releases — CI-style gating for model updates". They emphasized low-latency streaming (editor insert speed), ability to pin a model family per workspace, and deterministic evals to avoid regressions.

Details / friction points (shorthand):
- Workload: interactive completion + multi-line snippet streaming; heavy tail of short (<=128 tokens) completions but occasional long generation for refactors.
- Performance target: 30-50 ms token generation P95 for typical completions; max 120 ms P95 for 4k context refactor flows.
- Throughput: simultaneous 200 concurrent editors in peak internal alpha; expect burstiness during demo windows.
- Reproducibility: require model version pin + seed control + CV-style eval gates that run on a labeled prompt set before rollout.
- Rollouts: want A/B canaries by org/workspace, automatic rollback on quality regression or latency SLO breach. Also want traffic split and gradual ramping.
- Eval gates: quality measured by n-gram overlap + semantic unit tests + language-aware linting (no harmful rewrites). Need webhook for test failures.

What we demoed/asked:
- Can Redwood pin exact model commit/quantization profile? (Yes, they asked for commit-level pinning.)
- Can we run canaries segmented by org and route fallback to a smaller quantized variant? (High interest.)
- How does KV cache behave across model variant switch? They want no correctness regression.

Decision criteria (quoted): "If we can run a reproducible canary that proves no semantic regressions and meet latency targets at scale, we buy Dedicated + optimize." 

Next tacticals: provide canary run playbook, sample eval set (will send by 2026-03-12), proposed SLA for KMS + residency. Legal to follow up on RD-3150 for KMS integration.
